scope: Primary documents personally read at recorded locators; the original-source locator index was used only to locate possible sources. This reviewer fetched these authoritative URLs independently.

sources.title: Python 3.13.5 reference: slicings
sources.authority_reason: Python language maintainers own the language reference.
sources.inspection_note: Read Slicings lines 952–1004: lower/upper/stride form slice objects, comma-separated indices form a tuple. This specifies syntax; concrete tensor dispatch is also executed.

sources.title: Python 3.13.5 built-in sequence slicing
sources.authority_reason: Python maintainers publish the standard type contracts.
sources.inspection_note: Read common sequence operations note (4), lines 1060–1066: i <= k < j. Supports exclusive stop for [4:12]; tensor behavior is additionally run.

sources.title: PyTorch torch.sum official installed-revision API docstring
sources.authority_reason: Immutable upstream PyTorch source at torch.version.git_version.
sources.inspection_note: Read add_docstr(torch.sum), lines 11266–11292: sum with no dim sums all input elements. Boolean mask count and scalar int conversion are verified by running the literal fence.

sources.title: Pillow 12.3.0 Image.crop and Image.resize
sources.authority_reason: Original image-operation implementation maintained by the Pillow project.
sources.inspection_note: Read Image.crop/_crop lines 1369–1414 and resize lines 2329–2369. Crop returns a rectangle; resize consumes its supplied source, requested size is width/height, RGB default is BICUBIC. These operations do not take missing original pixels as extra inputs.

sources.title: Pillow 12.3.0 handbook: resampling filters
sources.authority_reason: Official Pillow handbook describing the implementation filter contracts.
sources.inspection_note: Read resampling section lines 162–208: geometric operations may map multiple inputs to one output; BOX uses equal weights, bilinear/cubic combine contributing pixels; nearest picks one and ignores the others. Supports possibility of small feature/background mixing, not every filter doing averaging.

sources.title: VizWiz Grand Challenge: Answering Visual Questions from Blind People
sources.version: Gurari et al., CVPR 2018 published proceedings PDF, pp. 3608–3617
sources.authority_reason: Original authors’ peer-reviewed paper hosted by the official CVF proceedings archive.
sources.inspection_note: Read PDF pp. 1–2 Abstract/Introduction, p. 3 Section 2 Answerability Visual Questions, pp. 4–5 Section 3.3 Collecting Answers (text extraction order crosses columns). Missing content can make questions unanswerable; annotation instructions permit Unanswerable when answer cannot be obtained from the image. No VizWiz performance statistic is imported into this lesson.
